Each term is said in a sentence or two, with a link to the page that explains
it in full.

## Calculations {#analysis}

[Electrostatic]{#term-electrostatic}: a calculation of the charge on each
conductor for given voltages; it returns a capacitance matrix. See
[the problems](../concepts/problems.qmd#capacitance-charge-response-to-conductor-voltage).

[Eigenmode]{#term-eigenmode}: a calculation of the resonant modes of a model,
each with its frequency, Q and fields. A mode is not a driven response. See
[the problems](../concepts/problems.qmd#resonance-modes-of-a-field-and-circuit-model).

[Driven Terminal]{#term-driven-terminal}: the HFSS calculation that excites
ports referenced to conductors and returns complex S-parameters.

[Driven Modal]{#term-driven-modal}: the HFSS calculation with modal ports.
SCGSim does not offer it in this version
([Not supported](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#current-exclusions)).

## Layout and plan {#geometry-and-workflow}

[Entity]{#term-entity}: one named piece of the layout, such as a pad or a
ground plane, identified by its path in the assembly (`chip/q0/pad`). See
[Source identity, Occurrence and Net](../concepts/geometry.qmd#entity-occurrence-and-net).

[Occurrence]{#term-occurrence}: one placement of a component in the layout.
Two placements of one component are two occurrences, with their own Entity
paths.

[Net]{#term-net}: a set of Entities that you declare to be one conductor, with
`plan.set_nets`. SCGSim never makes a Net from shapes that touch.

[Ground]{#term-ground}: the choice of which conductor, or which outer face, is
held at 0 V in a calculation. It is not the same as a Net named "ground" or a
solver's own ground type; each calculation states how it sets it.

[Region]{#term-region}: a volume of the model that is not metal: the substrate,
a dielectric, or the vacuum region, the box of empty space around the model.

[GeometryPlan]{#term-geometry-plan}: the object you build in a notebook from
the layout, its layer stack, the Nets, the vacuum region and the Surface-EPR
films; every simulation takes it. See [GeometryPlan and SGB](specs/geometry-plan.qmd).

[Snapshot]{#term-snapshot}: the frozen copy of a plan that `plan.prepare()`
returns, with no live link to the layout. A simulation takes a snapshot with
`set_plan`; to change anything, prepare a new one.

[SGB]{#term-sgb}: SCGSim's geometry builder, which turns a snapshot into the 3D
model every solver uses.

[Sidecar]{#term-sidecar}: the file SGB writes beside the model that records
which face and volume of the model came from which Entity, Net and band.

## Geometry {#geometry}

[Body]{#term-body}: a piece of geometry in a source or a model. Whether it
becomes a sheet or a solid depends on the route; Body alone does not say.

[Sheet]{#term-sheet}: a surface of zero thickness, such as a metal film on
Route A or a port sheet.

[Solid]{#term-solid}: a volume; in AEDT, the representation `modeling="solid"`
selects, in which each film keeps its thickness.

[Thin Film]{#term-thin-film}: in AEDT, the representation `modeling="thin_film"`
selects, in which each film becomes a sheet. See
[Solid or thin_film](specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#aedt-solid-thin-film).

[Route A and Route B]{#term-route}: the two ways a Palace model represents
metal. Route A makes each film a zero-thickness perfect-conductor sheet; Route
B keeps each conductor a finite volume whose surface is a perfect conductor.
You choose with `sim.set_route("A")` or `"B"` (the default). See
[Route A and Route B](../concepts/routes.qmd).

[Port]{#term-port}: a sheet across a gap where a circuit element, a junction or
an excitation is attached.

[Terminal]{#term-terminal}: in a capacitance calculation, a conductor set to
1 V in turn; in HFSS Driven Terminal, the conductor edge a port excites
against its reference.

## Surface EPR {#surface-epr-terms}

[Surface EPR]{#term-surface-epr}: the share of a mode's electric energy that
would sit in a thin lossy film on a surface of the model, estimated from the
field at that surface. See [Surface EPR](../concepts/surface-epr.qmd).

[MA, MS, SA]{#term-ma-ms-sa}: the three kinds of film surface: metal-air (MA),
metal-substrate (MS) and substrate-air (SA).

[Gap edge]{#term-gap-edge}: an edge of a conductor that faces exposed
substrate. Bands are measured from gap edges.

[Inset margin]{#term-inset-margin}: a distance from the gap edges, in µm. A
margin row of Surface EPR counts only the part of a surface at least that far
from a gap edge. The rows of different margins overlap; never add them.

[Band]{#term-band}: a strip of a surface between two margins, cut into the
model so that its participation can be integrated. Margins of 0.5 and 1.0 µm
give bands from 0 to 0.5 µm and 0.5 to 1.0 µm.

[EPR]{#term-epr}: energy participation ratio: the energy in one part of the
model divided by the model's normalization energy. Thin-film estimates are not
added to that denominator. See
[normalization](../concepts/surface-epr.qmd#quantities-and-normalization).

[SPR]{#term-spr}: surface participation ratio: the estimated energy in one
interface film divided by the stated normalization energy. It is an estimate of
an interface, not a disjoint part of the total energy.

EPR and SPR are dimensionless ratios. They are not percentages, and not loss:
a loss contribution such as inverse-Q also needs a loss tangent.

## Mesh and convergence {#mesh-and-convergence}

[Mesh]{#term-mesh}: the tetrahedra the field solver computes on. A mesh
summary tells you the size of the mesh, not whether the answer is accurate.

[Adaptive pass]{#term-adaptive-pass}: one solve in a run that refines its mesh
between solves; pass 1 solves the first mesh.

[AMR]{#term-amr}: adaptive mesh refinement: the solver refines the mesh where
its error estimate is largest, between passes.

[Nonconformal AMR]{#term-nonconformal-amr}: AMR that may refine an element
without refining its neighbours, leaving hanging nodes; Palace's
`Model.Refinement.Nonconformal`. See [MFEM's explanation](https://mfem.org/howto/ncmesh/).

[Convergence]{#term-convergence}: whether the quantities you declared changed
less than your thresholds from pass to pass. See
[the declaration](specs/palace-electrostatic-sgb.qmd#convergence-declaration).

## Running {#running}

[Solver]{#term-solver}: the program that computes the fields: Palace, or HFSS,
Q3D and Q2D in AEDT.

[Handoff]{#term-handoff}: the folder a simulation prepares for a solver run:
the model, the solver input and a run script. Preparing a handoff does not run
the solver.

[Run folder]{#term-run-folder}: the folder a simulation writes its mesh,
configuration and handoff into and the solver writes its results into; code
calls it `run_dir`. Results are read from a run folder. A *package* is the
`.tar.gz` archive of a run folder, made to carry it to another host.

## Results {#results}

[C]{#term-c} is capacitance, [G]{#term-g} conductance. [RLGC]{#term-rlgc}: the
resistance, inductance, conductance and capacitance of a line, per unit length.

[Maxwell capacitance matrix]{#term-maxwell-capacitance-matrix}: the matrix
that gives each conductor's charge from the conductor voltages. Its diagonal
holds each conductor's total capacitance and its off-diagonal elements are
negative couplings. Keep its conductor order and units.

## Symbols and units {#symbols-and-units}

Capacitance is in farads (`F`) or femtofarads (`fF`): 1 fF = 10⁻¹⁵ F. A ratio
has no unit; parts per million (`ppm`) count it in millionths, 1 ppm = 10⁻⁶. SCGSim's APIs do
not all use one unit: lengths are in micrometres, Palace frequencies in hertz
when you set them and GHz in results, AEDT frequencies in GHz, and film
thicknesses in metres (`film_thickness_m`) or model units (`thickness`). Each
API states its own.
